chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction Organisations that operate under external supervision inherited their release controls from an era in which software shipped twice a year. A committee met, read a written description of the intended change, and recorded a decision in minutes. That arrangement made sense when a release was a rare and expensive event. It fits badly with a team that merges to the trunk forty times a week, because the committee becomes either a rubber stamp or a queue, and both outcomes destroy the control it was meant to provide. The interesting question is therefore not whether approval should exist, but what an approval is evidence of. A supervisor does not care that a named person clicked a button; the supervisor cares that the change was reviewed by someone other than its author, that the review was recorded, and that the recording cannot be altered after the fact. Each of those properties can be produced by a pipeline more reliably than by a meeting. The remainder of this text describes how the three properties survive the move from a committee to an automated delivery path, and where the translation genuinely fails rather than merely feeling unfamiliar. The failures matter more than the successes, because a control that has been automated badly is harder to notice than one that was never automated at all. 2 Segregation Of Duties The oldest of the three properties is the requirement that the person who writes a change must not be the person who releases it. In a manual world this was enforced by handing a deployment package to a separate operations group. The rule is cheap to state and surprisingly hard to enforce, because identity leaks. The usual design lets an on-call engineer bypass the approval requirement, with the obligation to obtain a retrospective review within a stated period. In practice two failure modes dominate. The first is volume: when the ordinary path is slow, teams reclassify routine work as urgent, and the exception becomes the norm. A regime in which a fifth of all changes travel the emergency path has not got an emergency path, it has got a second ordinary path with no review. The second failure mode is closure. The retrospective review is created as a ticket, the ticket ages, and no mechanism forces it shut. Counting open retrospective reviews is a better indicator of the health of a release process than counting approvals granted, because the number rises quietly and nobody is accountable for it. A useful rule is to make the emergency path deliberately more expensive in attention rather than in time: it should be fast to invoke and impossible to forget, for instance by blocking the next ordinary release of the same component until the retrospective review has been closed.

chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction A modern application is assembled rather than written. The proportion of shipped bytes that originate in the repository of the team that ships them is small, often under five per cent, and the remainder arrives through a dependency resolver from registries that the team does not operate and cannot inspect. This changes the nature of the question an operator must answer after a vulnerability is announced. The question is no longer whether the team wrote faulty code; it is whether a particular version of a particular component is present in something currently running, and if so, where. Answering that question by searching source repositories is unreliable, because the resolver may have selected a transitive version that appears in no manifest a human ever wrote. Answering it by scanning production hosts is slow and covers only what is still running, not what shipped last week and was rolled back. The durable answer is an inventory produced by the build itself, at the moment the artefact is created, listing what actually went in. Everything that follows depends on that inventory being generated by the build rather than described by a person, because a description written by a person records intent while a build records fact, and the interesting incidents live exactly in the gap between the two. 2 Generating A Component Inventory The inventory must be produced where the resolution happens. A tool that reads the manifest files in the repository reproduces the intent of the developer and misses everything the resolver decided, including version substitutions, platform specific packages, and components vendored into a base image years ago by someone who has since left. A tool that inspects the finished artefact sees what is really there but loses the link back to a source, which is precisely the link an investigation needs. The workable compromise is to instrument the build so that the resolver reports its decisions, and to combine that report with an inspection of the finished artefact, treating a discrepancy between the two as a defect rather than as noise. The comparison is noisier than it sounds. Component names are not standardised across ecosystems, so the same library appears under three spellings and a naive match misses two of them. chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction An outage is an unplanned experiment on a system that nobody understood as well as they believed. The review that follows is worth conducting only if it changes something, and most reviews change nothing because they conclude with a finding that a person made a mistake. That conclusion is almost always true and almost never useful, because the same conditions will produce the same mistake from a different person next quarter. The alternative approach starts from the assumption that everyone involved acted reasonably given the information available to them at the time, and asks what made the wrong action look reasonable. That reframing is not a courtesy extended to the people involved; it is the only framing that produces findings a team can act on, because it directs attention to the signals, defaults, and time pressures that shaped the decision rather than to the decision itself. It is also fragile. A review conducted in this style inside an organisation that later uses its findings in a performance assessment will produce exactly one honest review, and every subsequent one will be written defensively. The technique and the guarantee that surrounds it cannot be separated, and an organisation that adopts the first without the second gets worse information than it had before. 2 Detection And Escalation Most of the elapsed time in a serious incident is spent before anyone knows there is an incident. Reducing detection time is therefore mostly a matter of measuring outcomes at the edge rather than health in the middle. Escalation has the opposite problem: it is usually fast enough and far too broad. Its purpose is not measurement; it is the pre-negotiation of a decision that is otherwise made under pressure, badly, by whoever is loudest during the outage. chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction When the configuration of a system is written down in files and applied by a tool, the files become a claim about the world rather than a description of it. The claim holds only as long as nothing changes the world by another route. Something always does. An engineer resizes a disk during a night shift because the alternative is data loss and the ordinary path takes two hours. A support process adjusts a firewall rule to unblock a customer. An automated remediation script restarts a component with different arguments. Each of these actions is defensible in isolation, and each moves the running system away from what the files describe. The divergence is not a discipline problem to be solved by forbidding manual action, because forbidding it merely relocates the action to a route with no record at all. It is a measurement problem: the organisation needs to know continuously how far apart the two states are, which differences are deliberate, and which appeared without anyone deciding. It holds the credentials needed to reach every environment the organisation runs, it executes code that changes on every commit, and it is operated by a team whose primary concern is throughput. Anyone who can influence what the pipeline executes can, in most default configurations, read everything it can reach. Der übliche Ausweg besteht darin, die Abschätzung jährlich zu wiederholen. Das erzeugt Aufwand ohne Erkenntnis, denn eine jährliche Prüfung findet die Abweichung im Mittel ein halbes Jahr nach ihrem Entstehen. Diese Aussage ist juristisch unstrittig und betrieblich folgenlos geblieben, solange niemand danach gefragt hat, was in einem ausgelieferten Stand eigentlich enthalten ist. Der Unterschied ist erheblich. Sorgfalt bei der Auswahl lässt sich durch eine Richtlinie belegen, die vorschreibt, welche Bezugsquellen zulässig sind. Kenntnis des Bestands lässt sich nur durch eine Aufstellung belegen, die zum Zeitpunkt der Erstellung des Artefakts entsteht und die tatsächlich eingegangenen Bestandteile nennt, einschließlich derjenigen, die niemand bewusst ausgewählt hat. chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction Standing access accumulates. A person joins a team and receives the rights that team needs, moves to another team and receives a second set, and the first set is never withdrawn because withdrawing it requires someone to notice. After three moves the individual holds a combination of rights that no policy would ever have granted deliberately, and that combination is invisible because each grant was individually justified at the time it was made. The periodic review exists to catch this accumulation. It works by presenting a list of who holds what to a person who is supposed to know whether that is still appropriate, and recording the answer. Almost every implementation of this control fails in the same way, and the failure is worth describing precisely because it is so uniform. The reviewer is shown several hundred entries of the form account, resource, level, is given a deadline, and approves all of them within a few minutes. The record produced is formally complete and evidentially worthless, and the organisation has spent real effort obtaining a signature that means nothing. 2 Making The Review Answerable The defect is not laziness on the part of the reviewer; it is that the question asked cannot be answered from the information supplied. A line that says this account may write to that repository does not tell the reviewer whether the person has used the right in the last year, why it was granted, or what would break if it were removed. Supplying those three facts changes the exercise entirely. Usage in particular is decisive: an entry that has not been exercised in twelve months can be proposed for removal by default, with the reviewer confirming exceptions rather than approving the whole list. This inverts the effort so that attention goes to the small set of unusual cases instead of being spread evenly and uselessly across everything. It also requires that access is logged with enough fidelity to distinguish use from non-use, which many systems do not do by default and which is usually the first genuine piece of work in such a programme. 3

chunks.chunk_text: 1 Introduction Instrumentation is added on the assumption that more recorded detail is always better, and the assumption holds until the invoice arrives. Retained telemetry has three costs that are usually accounted separately and therefore never compared: storage, which is small and visible; ingestion and indexing, which is large and visible; and the obligation attached to holding the data, which is invisible until an incident or a request makes it concrete. The third cost dominates in the long run and is the one nobody models. A record of every request served, retained for two years, is a liability as well as an asset: it must be secured, it can be compelled, and it will be searched by someone whose purpose differs from the purpose for which it was collected. Deciding what to keep is therefore not a budget exercise but a design decision about what questions the organisation intends to be able to answer, and for how long it intends to remain answerable for them. 2 Deciding What To Keep A useful discipline is to state, for each stream, the question it exists to answer and the age beyond which the answer stops mattering. Debugging streams answer questions about the last few hours and can be discarded within a week without any loss anyone will notice. Capacity streams answer questions about seasonal shape and need a year, but only in aggregated form, at a resolution far coarser than the raw record. Audit streams answer questions years later and must be retained in full, but they are a tiny fraction of the volume and are usually the only stream with a defensible retention period. Applying this classification typically removes most of the volume and almost none of the value. Capacity streams answer questions about seasonal shape and need a year, but only in aggregated form, at a resolution far coarser than the raw record. Audit streams answer questions years later and must be retained in full, but they are a tiny fraction of the volume and are usually the only stream with a defensible retention period. Applying this classification typically removes most of the volume and almost none of the value. The reason it is rarely applied is that the classification has to be made per stream by someone who understands the stream, and the effort falls on teams that see no benefit from it, while the cost falls on a central budget nobody defends line by line. 3 Deletion That Actually Happens A retention period that is written down

Each of these is a route by which data survives its own retention rule, and none of them is visible from the system that believes it deleted the record. Sein Wert bemisst sich deshalb nicht daran, wie sorgfältig er entsteht, sondern daran, ob er zum Zeitpunkt der Frage noch existiert und noch lesbar ist. Beides wird beim Aufbau eines Freigabeverfahrens fast nie mitgedacht, weil die Aufmerksamkeit der Beteiligten dem Vorgang gilt und nicht seinem Nachleben. Typisch ist folgende Lage: Der Nachweis liegt in dem Werkzeug, das die Freigabe verwaltet, dieses Werkzeug wird nach vier Jahren durch ein anderes ersetzt, und die Übernahme der Altdaten unterbleibt, weil sie im Migrationsprojekt keinen Fürsprecher hat. Danach ist der Nachweis nicht gelöscht, sondern unerreichbar, was in der Wirkung dasselbe ist und in der Darstellung nach außen schlechter aussieht, weil niemand erklären kann, wo er geblieben ist. 2 Format und Ablageort Ein Nachweis, der nur im Zusammenspiel mit der Datenbank seines Ursprungswerkzeugs verständlich ist, überlebt dieses Werkzeug nicht.
